name: Udihe
confidence_why: Every source puts the main stress on the last syllable by default, but Nikolaeva and Tolskaya 2001 (restated in Tolskaya 2011 and adopted by Schiering and van der Hulst 2010) move it to the rightmost long or laryngealized vowel when the word has one, while the older Russian descriptions in Sunik 1968 and Kormushin 1998, which Gordon 2002 and StressTyp2 follow, give a weight-insensitive final stress with a weak initial stress.
catalog_quote: The stress is quantity-sensitive and falls on the most right bimoraic vowel or, in the absence of bimoraic vowels, on the most right vowel in the word. In affixes, word-final high vowels are extrametrical with respect to stress.

tone_statements.citation: Kazama, Shinjiro. 2022. A Grammar of Udihe. Shigen: Tōkyō Gaikokugo Daigaku Kijutsu Gengogaku Ronshū (思言 東京外国語大学記述言語学論集) 18: 3-42. Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
tone_statements.quote: Like other Tungusic languages, most Udihe words tend to place the primary stress on the first syllable. For an analysis of tone existence in Udihe, see Janhunen (1999).

tone_statements.citation: Kuznetsova, Natalia. 2022 [vol. dated 2023]. Vowel aspiration and glottalisation across Udihe dialects: Phonetics, phonology, evolution, typology. In Elia Dal Corso & Soung-U Kim (eds.), Language Endangerment and Obsolescence in East Asia: China, Japan, Siberia, and Taiwan, 6-58. Leiden: Brill. DOI 10.1163/9789004523944_003.
tone_statements.quote: Udihe glottalisation at present shares some structural properties of lexical tone: it is a local vowel-long phenomenon and carries a distinctive function. As mentioned in §5, Janhunen has tried to equal length and “phonations” in Udihe to tones. However, at the present state of development, Udihe vowel length and glottalisation can hardly be defined as tones, at least according to the most common definitions of the term “tone”. The main reason is that pitch movement is not their primary phonetic cue … glottalisation tends to disappear from Udihe altogether rather than evolving into true tone.
tone_statements.summary: Not tonal: vowel glottalisation and length are a stod-like 'neither stress nor tone' laryngeal prosody cued by creak, not pitch; Janhunen's four-tone analysis rejected; lexical stress itself doubtful.

tone_statements.citation: Perekhvalskaya, Elena. 2022. From consonant to tone: Laryngealized and pharyngealized vowels in Udihe. In Andreas Hölzl & Thomas E. Payne (eds.), Tungusic languages: Past and present (Studies in Diversity Linguistics 32), 227-262. Berlin: Language Science Press.
tone_statements.quote: The term stress or accent is not appropriate here. It is the prosodic structure of the word that is contrastive: words with similar segmental chains can differ by their prosodic structure. Contrastive prosodic patterns depend on the presence of a laryngealized vowel and on its place in the word. Contrastive prosodic patterns are, in fact, linguistic tones. Thus, Udihe and especially its southern varieties became a tonal language of the type of languages with low tone density, like Scandinavian dialects or Latvian.
tone_statements.locator: p. 258, section 6 'Conclusions' (see also p. 249, section 4.4.2: 'only in the most innovative varieties of Bikin and Iman, it became the main (and in Iman Udihe the only) distinctive feature [+tone]. Thus, these varieties should be classified as tonal')
tone_statements.n_tones: One marked low/falling tone (on historically laryngealized long vowels) vs unma…

tone_statements.citation: Perekhvalskaya, Elena V. 2010. Aspirirovannye i glottalizovannye glasnye v dialektax udègejskogo jazyka [Aspirated and glottalized vowels in the dialects of Udihe]. Voprosy jazykoznanija 2010(6): 58-87.
tone_statements.quote: Даже в тех диалектах / идиолектах, где сегменты звучания полностью заменены супрасегментными характеристиками гласного, нельзя говорить о тонах в терминологическом смысле этого слова. О системе тонов говорят, когда каждый слог слова характеризуется определенным тоном, контурным или уровневым. В данном случае этого не происходит. … Таким образом, мы имеем дело с классическим случаем «слоговых акцентов» — в языке имеются разные типы ударения, как в современном литовском или во многих древних индоевропейских языках.
tone_statements.translation: Even in those dialects/idiolects where the sound segments are fully replaced by suprasegmental characteristics of the vowel, one cannot speak of tones in the terminological sense of the word. One speaks of a tone system when every syllable of the word carries a definite tone, contour or level. That is not the case here. … Thus we are dealing with a classic case of 'syllable accents': the language has different types of accent, as in modern Lithuanian or many ancient Indo-European languages.
tone_statements.locator: pp. 82-83, section 'Глоттализованные гласные как слоговые акценты'
tone_statements.summary: Denies a tone system; in some Bikin varieties old glottalized vowels are realised as a syllable accent (pitch drop plus intensity peak on one mora), likened to Lithuanian accent types.

sources.citation: Sunik, Orest P. (1968). Udegeyskij jazyk [The Udihe language]. In Jazyki narodov SSSR. Nauka. pp. 149-171.
sources.quote: Ударение в удэгейских словах как бы обрамляет слово: на первый слог падает слабое экспираторное ударение, а на последний слог — тоническое (или музыкальное). Гласный первого слога артикулируется поэтому наиболее отчетливо, а гласный последнего слога произносится с некоторым повышением тона, но очень часто с ослабленной, недостаточно ясной артикуляцией

sources.note: Read in the held scan (the Soviet sketch whose p. 213 sentence the catalog rows above carry in Russian and English). Basis: the author's 1964 fieldwork among the Khabarovsk-krai Udihe, checked at Gvasjugi on the Khor, plus Šnejder's materials; the description follows the Khor-Anjuj (northern) variety (fn. 1, p. 211), whereas the record's source describes Bikin (southern). States a quantity-insensitive frame - weak expiratory stress on the first syllable, tonic (musical) stress with a pitch rise on the last - with no long-vowel condition: not the weight rule the record codes from Nikolaeva & Tolskaya 2001:33. Gordon 2002 and StressTyp2 code this tradition as final primary + initial secondary. [tr.: 'Stress in Udihe words frames the word, as it were: a weak expiratory stress falls on the first syllable, and a tonic (or musical) one on the last syllable. The vowel of the first syllable is therefore articulated most distinctly, while the vowel of the last syllable is pronounced with some rise in pitch, but very often with weakened, insufficiently clear articulation.']

The stressed vowel is usually marked by greater intensity and sometimes by pitch raising and lengthening. ... Secondary stress is less intense and in polysyllabic words can fall on the last syllable. sources.citation: Kormushin, Igor Valentinovich. 1998. Udykheiskii (Udegeiskii) Iazyk. Moscow: Nauka.
sources.quote: Удыхейское слово обладает двояким ударением. На первом (корневом) слоге делается силовой акцент, это собственно ударение. Последний слог слова получает музыкальное повышение тона. Серединные слоги не претерпевают редукции, поэтому динамическое ударение первого слога не столь выделяется, как ударный слог в словах русского языка.

States a double stress with the force accent, 'the stress proper', on the first (root) syllable and a musical pitch rise on the last syllable, with no vowel-length condition: not the weight rule the record codes from Nikolaeva & Tolskaya 2001:33 (rightmost long or laryngealized vowel, else the final vowel). This is the description StressTyp2 and Gordon 2002:500 follow (coded there as quantity-insensitive final primary + initial secondary). [tr.: 'The Udihe word has a double stress. On the first (root) syllable a force accent is made; this is the stress proper. The last syllable of the word receives a musical rise in pitch. Medial syllables do not undergo reduction, so the dynamic stress of the first syllable does not stand out as much as the stressed syllable in Russian words.']

sources.quote: The term stress or accent is not appropriate here. It is the prosodic structure of the word that is contrastive: words with similar segmental chains can differ by their prosodic structure. Contrastive prosodic patterns depend on the presence of a laryngealized vowel and on its place in the word. Contrastive prosodic patterns are, in fact, linguistic tones. Thus, Udihe and especially its southern varieties became a tonal language of the type of languages with low tone density, like Scandinavian dialects or Latvian.

sources.note: Traces laryngealized (V'V < *V-k/q-V) and pharyngealized (VhV < *V-s-V) long vowels through the Udihe-Oroch dialect continuum as stages 'from consonant to tone': glottal stop > creaky phonation > high intensity with low/falling pitch. A pitch drop on the laryngealized vowel is found in all varieties; in the northern cluster (Xor, Anjuj) it is a side-effect of phonation, but in Bikin and Iman (and fully in Olon) creaky voice is lost in allegro speech and low/falling tone with raised intensity becomes the main or only distinctive feature, so these varieties 'should be classified as tonal' (p. 2…

sources.quote: Даже в тех диалектах / идиолектах, где сегменты звучания полностью заменены супрасегментными характеристиками гласного, нельзя говорить о тонах в терминологическом смысле этого слова. О системе тонов говорят, когда каждый слог слова характеризуется определенным тоном, контурным или уровневым. В данном случае этого не происходит. … Таким образом, мы имеем дело с классическим случаем «слоговых акцентов» — в языке имеются разные типы ударения, как в современном литовском или во многих древних индоевропейских языках.

tone.translation: Even in those dialects/idiolects where the sound segments are fully replaced by suprasegmental characteristics of the vowel, one cannot speak of tones in the terminological sense of the word. One speaks of a tone system when every syllable of the word carries a definite tone, contour or level. That is not the case here. … Thus we are dealing with a classic case of 'syllable accents': the language has different types of accent, as in modern Lithuanian or many ancient Indo-European languages.
